paragraphs.text: My brethren, hold not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, [the Lord] of glory, with respect of persons.
paragraphs.original: Ἀδελφοί μου, μὴ ἐν προσωπολημψίαις ἔχετε τὴν πίστιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῆς δόξης;
paragraphs.translit: Adelphoi mou, mē en prosōpolēmpsiais echete tēn pistin tou kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou tēs doxēs;

paragraphs.text: For if there come into your synagogue a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, and there come in also a poor man in vile clothing;
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν γὰρ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς συναγωγὴν ὑμῶν ἀνὴρ χρυσοδακτύλιος ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ, εἰσέλθῃ δὲ καὶ πτωχὸς ἐν ῥυπαρᾷ ἐσθῆτι,
paragraphs.translit: ean gar eiselthē eis synagōgēn hymōn anēr chrysodaktylios en esthēti lampra, eiselthē de kai ptōchos en rhypara esthēti,

paragraphs.text: and ye have regard to him that weareth the fine clothing, and say, Sit thou here in a good place; and ye say to the poor man, Stand thou there, or sit under my footstool;
paragraphs.original: ἐπιβλέψητε δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν φοροῦντα τὴν ἐσθῆτα τὴν λαμπρὰν καὶ εἴπητε· Σὺ κάθου ὧδε καλῶς, καὶ τῷ πτωχῷ εἴπητε· Σὺ στῆθι ἢ κάθου ἐκεῖ ὑπὸ τὸ ὑποπόδιόν μου,
paragraphs.translit: epiblepsēte de epi ton phorounta tēn esthēta tēn lampran kai eipēte· Sy kathou hōde kalōs, kai tō ptōchō eipēte· Sy stēthi ē kathou ekei hypo to hypopodion mou,

paragraphs.text: Do ye not make distinctions among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?
paragraphs.original: οὐ διεκρίθητε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐγένεσθε κριταὶ διαλογισμῶν πονηρῶν;
paragraphs.translit: ou diekrithēte en heautois kai egenesthe kritai dialogismōn ponērōn;

paragraphs.text: Hearken, my beloved brethren; did not God choose them that are poor as to the world [to be] rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he promised to them that love him?
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσατε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί. οὐχ ὁ θεὸς ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πτωχοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ πλουσίους ἐν πίστει καὶ κληρονόμους τῆς βασιλείας ἧς ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν;
paragraphs.translit: akousate, adelphoi mou agapētoi. ouch ho theos exelexato tous ptōchous tō kosmō plousious en pistei kai klēronomous tēs basileias hēs epēngeilato tois agapōsin auton;

paragraphs.text: But ye have dishonored the poor man. Do not the rich oppress you, and themselves drag you before the judgment-seats?
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠτιμάσατε τὸν πτωχόν. οὐχ οἱ πλούσιοι καταδυναστεύουσιν ὑμῶν, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἕλκουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς κριτήρια;
paragraphs.translit: hymeis de ētimasate ton ptōchon. ouch hoi plousioi katadynasteuousin hymōn, kai autoi helkousin hymas eis kritēria;

paragraphs.text: Do not they blaspheme the honorable name by which ye are called?
paragraphs.original: οὐκ αὐτοὶ βλασφημοῦσιν τὸ καλὸν ὄνομα τὸ ἐπικληθὲν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς;
paragraphs.translit: ouk autoi blasphēmousin to kalon onoma to epiklēthen ephʼ hymas;

paragraphs.text: Howbeit if ye fulfil the royal law, according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself, ye do well:
paragraphs.original: Εἰ μέντοι νόμον τελεῖτε βασιλικὸν κατὰ τὴν γραφήν Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε·
paragraphs.translit: Ei mentoi nomon teleite basilikon kata tēn graphēn Agapēseis ton plēsion sou hōs seauton, kalōs poieite·

paragraphs.text: but if ye have respect of persons, ye commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ προσωπολημπτεῖτε, ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζεσθε, ἐλεγχόμενοι ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου ὡς παραβάται.
paragraphs.translit: ei de prosōpolēmpteite, hamartian ergazesthe, elenchomenoi hypo tou nomou hōs parabatai.

paragraphs.text: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet stumble in one [point], he is become guilty of all.
paragraphs.original: ὅστις γὰρ ὅλον τὸν νόμον τηρήσῃ, πταίσῃ δὲ ἐν ἑνί, γέγονεν πάντων ἔνοχος.
paragraphs.translit: hostis gar holon ton nomon tērēsē, ptaisē de en heni, gegonen pantōn enochos.

paragraphs.text: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou dost not commit adultery, but killest, thou art become a transgressor of the law.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ εἰπών· Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς εἶπεν καί· Μὴ φονεύσῃς· εἰ δὲ οὐ μοιχεύεις φονεύεις δέ, γέγονας παραβάτης νόμου.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar eipōn· Mē moicheusēs eipen kai· Mē phoneusēs· ei de ou moicheueis phoneueis de, gegonas parabatēs nomou.

paragraphs.text: So speak ye, and so do, as men that are to be judged by a law of liberty.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως λαλεῖτε καὶ οὕτως ποιεῖτε ὡς διὰ νόμου ἐλευθερίας μέλλοντες κρίνεσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs laleite kai houtōs poieite hōs dia nomou eleutherias mellontes krinesthai.

paragraphs.text: For judgment [is] without mercy to him that hath showed no mercy: mercy glorieth against judgment.
paragraphs.original: ἡ γὰρ κρίσις ἀνέλεος τῷ μὴ ποιήσαντι ἔλεος· κατακαυχᾶται ἔλεος κρίσεως.
paragraphs.translit: hē gar krisis aneleos tō mē poiēsanti eleos· katakauchatai eleos kriseōs.

paragraphs.text: What doth it profit, my brethren, if a man say he hath faith, but have not works? can that faith save him?
paragraphs.original: Τί ὄφελος, ἀδελφοί μου, ἐὰν πίστιν λέγῃ τις ἔχειν ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχῃ; μὴ δύναται ἡ πίστις σῶσαι αὐτόν;
paragraphs.translit: Ti ophelos, adelphoi mou, ean pistin legē tis echein erga de mē echē; mē dynatai hē pistis sōsai auton;

paragraphs.text: If a brother or sister be naked and in lack of daily food,
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἀδελφὴ γυμνοὶ ὑπάρχωσιν καὶ λειπόμενοι τῆς ἐφημέρου τροφῆς,
paragraphs.translit: ean adelphos ē adelphē gymnoi hyparchōsin kai leipomenoi tēs ephēmerou trophēs,

paragraphs.text: and one of you say unto them, Go in peace, be ye warmed and filled; and yet ye give them not the things needful to the body; what doth it profit?
paragraphs.original: εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν· Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ, θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε, μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος, τί ὄφελος;
paragraphs.translit: eipē de tis autois ex hymōn· Hypagete en eirēnē, thermainesthe kai chortazesthe, mē dōte de autois ta epitēdeia tou sōmatos, ti ophelos;

paragraphs.text: Even so faith, if it have not works, is dead in itself.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις, ἐὰν μὴ ἔχῃ ἔργα, νεκρά ἐστιν καθʼ ἑαυτήν.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hē pistis, ean mē echē erga, nekra estin kathʼ heautēn.

paragraphs.text: Yea, a man will say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: show me thy faith apart from [thy] works, and I by my works will show thee [my] faith.
paragraphs.original: Ἀλλʼ ἐρεῖ τις· Σὺ πίστιν ἔχεις κἀγὼ ἔργα ἔχω. δεῖξόν μοι τὴν πίστιν σου χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων, κἀγώ σοι δείξω ἐκ τῶν ἔργων μου τὴν πίστιν.
paragraphs.translit: Allʼ erei tis· Sy pistin echeis kagō erga echō. deixon moi tēn pistin sou chōris tōn ergōn, kagō soi deixō ek tōn ergōn mou tēn pistin.

paragraphs.text: Thou believest that God is one; thou doest well: the demons also believe, and shudder.
paragraphs.original: σὺ πιστεύεις ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν ὁ θεός; καλῶς ποιεῖς· καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια πιστεύουσιν καὶ φρίσσουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: sy pisteueis hoti heis estin ho theos; kalōs poieis· kai ta daimonia pisteuousin kai phrissousin.

paragraphs.text: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith apart from works is barren?
paragraphs.original: θέλεις δὲ γνῶναι, ὦ ἄνθρωπε κενέ, ὅτι ἡ πίστις χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων ἀργή ἐστιν;
paragraphs.translit: theleis de gnōnai, ō anthrōpe kene, hoti hē pistis chōris tōn ergōn argē estin;

paragraphs.text: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son upon the altar?
paragraphs.original: Ἀβραὰμ ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἀνενέγκας Ἰσαὰκ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον;
paragraphs.translit: Abraam ho patēr hēmōn ouk ex ergōn edikaiōthē, anenenkas Isaak ton hyion autou epi to thysiastērion;

paragraphs.text: Thou seest that faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect;
paragraphs.original: βλέπεις ὅτι ἡ πίστις συνήργει τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἡ πίστις ἐτελειώθη,
paragraphs.translit: blepeis hoti hē pistis synērgei tois ergois autou kai ek tōn ergōn hē pistis eteleiōthē,

paragraphs.text: and the scripture was fulfilled which saith, And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned unto him for righteousness; and he was called the friend of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπληρώθη ἡ γραφὴ ἡ λέγουσα· Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην, καὶ φίλος θεοῦ ἐκλήθη.
paragraphs.translit: kai eplērōthē hē graphē hē legousa· Episteusen de Abraam tō theō, kai elogisthē autō eis dikaiosynēn, kai philos theou eklēthē.

paragraphs.text: Ye see that by works a man is justified, and not only by faith.
paragraphs.original: ὁρᾶτε ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος καὶ οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως μόνον.
paragraphs.translit: horate hoti ex ergōn dikaioutai anthrōpos kai ouk ek pisteōs monon.

paragraphs.text: And in like manner was not also Rahab the harlot justified by works, in that she received the messengers, and sent them out another way?
paragraphs.original: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ὑποδεξαμένη τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ ἑτέρᾳ ὁδῷ ἐκβαλοῦσα;
paragraphs.translit: homoiōs de kai Rhaab hē pornē ouk ex ergōn edikaiōthē, hypodexamenē tous angelous kai hetera hodō ekbalousa;

paragraphs.text: For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, even so faith apart from works is dead.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα χωρὶς πνεύματος νεκρόν ἐστιν, οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις χωρὶς ἔργων νεκρά ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar to sōma chōris pneumatos nekron estin, houtōs kai hē pistis chōris ergōn nekra estin.
